page: The Vultr vx1-m-48c-384gb is an x86_64 cloud server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. The architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration. It is configured with 384 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without bundled hardware GPUs.

Benchmark measurements place the vx1-m-48c-384gb in the upper performance tier for processing and throughput. It achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 26198.0 and a single-core score of 2758.0, both landing in the top 10 percent of recorded results. Software compilation using Clang reached a top-tier score of 58607.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth registered at 395.69 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 231.13 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top decile. In database operations, the server attained strong tier rankings with 30353.44 operations in PassMark database tests and 87.64 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The high memory-to-core allocation provides solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks, consolidating large datasets without the overhead of distributing across multiple smaller nodes. However, with only 1 GB of local NVMe storage, persistent applications require external storage attachments. Large language model inference scales well for smaller models (reaching 3890.79 prompt tokens per second on 135M models), but drops to average tier speeds on 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators. This instance is best suited for in-memory databases, Clang-based CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, and large data-processing pipelines.
